title: Per-tenant embedding endpoint (embedding_base_url) + config-time dimension probe with legible remediation
background: The embedding endpoint is server-wide: config/runtime.exs:382-385 sets %{base_url: OPENAI_BASE_URL || "https://api.openai.com/v1", model: ...}, read at knowledge/embedding_client.ex:194 (@default_base_url at :41, provider_config/0 at :295). Per-tenant configuration today (llm/tenant_llm_settings.ex:41-54) covers api_key, extraction_model, classification_model, merge_model, embedding_api_key, embedding_model - key and model, but NOT endpoint. Importantly the embedding KEY is already per-tenant and MANDATORY (embedding_client.ex:58-60,75-77; the global operator key was deliberately removed in runtime.exs:375-381), so the per-tenant credential plumbing and its MCP surface (set_llm_config) already exist. Adding the endpoint is one field plus one read - not a subsystem. TWO grounded constraints the 39 draft missed: (1) the set_llm_config surface is ROLE :user, not agent - router.ex:185-189 puts PATCH /tenants/me/llm-config in the :user scope with an explicit comment that the PATCH stores a tenant secret, and mcp-server/index.js:1836-1843 sends the exact LOOPCTL_USER_KEY with the global-key override bypassed (reviews #12/#13). (2) UrlGuard.pin/1 (net/url_guard.ex, GHSA-jh42-wf7g-f5rg) unconditionally blocks loopback, 10/8, 100.64/10, 169.254/16 and Fly 6PN - i.e. exactly where a local Ollama or TEI lives - and accepts only a :schemes option, so 'just reuse UrlGuard' does not compose with a local endpoint.

story.as_a: an agent configuring a tenant that must not send content to third-party providers
story.i_want_to: set the tenant's embedding endpoint to a local or self-chosen OpenAI-compatible server through the same MCP tool already used for the key, and be told immediately if the endpoint is unusable
story.so_that: embeddings are computed where the tenant chooses, and a misconfiguration fails at config time with a fix I can act on - not hours later as an opaque write error

rationale: This is the smallest change that makes the hosted service usable for a privacy-constrained tenant, and it is the prerequisite for the egress guard in US-41.4 (there is nothing to point at until an endpoint is configurable). The probe exists because loopctl has NO UI: a human would notice a broken endpoint in a settings screen, an agent will not unless the tool tells it.

acceptance_criteria.description: tenant_llm_settings gains embedding_base_url (nullable; NULL means fall back to the server-wide default, preserving today's behavior exactly). The RESOLUTION POINT is named explicitly: Llm.resolve/2's returned map gains :base_url (it returns only %{api_key, model} today, embedding_client.ex:58-80), and the arity-zero embeddings_url/0 (embedding_client.ex:193) is replaced by that resolved value. A test asserts BOTH post paths - do_post/single (embedding_client.ex:86) AND do_post_batch (:100) - hit the tenant endpoint, so one path cannot be fixed while the other silently calls the vendor default.

The field is writable through the EXISTING set_llm_config MCP tool and its matching JSON API endpoint - no new tool, no UI - and that surface REMAINS role :user (router.ex:185-189, LlmConfigController's RequireRole). The epic's agent-manageability audit is corrected accordingly: endpoint configuration is USER-write, not agent-write, because the same PATCH carries tenant secrets (api_key, embedding_api_key) and CLAUDE.md's role checklist forbids lowering a secret-bearing endpoint to :agent. If a genuinely agent-writable endpoint field is ever wanted it must be a SEPARATE non-secret route with its own AC and its own security argument - not a role downgrade on this one. A test asserts an agent-role key gets 403 on the endpoint write.

Config-time probe: setting embedding_base_url (or embedding_model) issues ONE test embedding against the supplied endpoint before persisting. On failure NOTHING is persisted and the call returns a legible, agent-readable error. On success the returned dimension is validated against the instance's published supported set (US-41.1 AC-41.1.3) and recorded as the tenant's PENDING dimension - never activated implicitly.

A dimension CHANGE is a gated, staged cutover, never a silent corpus blackhole. Because US-41.1 AC-41.1.10 excludes stale-dimension rows from recall, a probe that returns a dimension different from the tenant's current one must: (a) refuse unless the caller supplies an explicit acknowledgement/force flag, (b) report in meta how many article and memory rows will become stale, (c) record the new value as pending_dimension and enqueue the re-embed backfill, activating the new dimension only when the backfill reports completion, and (d) define in-flight Oban embedding job behavior - a job whose vector dimension no longer matches the pending target is tagged and retried against the pending dimension rather than written or silently discarded. A test asserts an un-acknowledged dimension change is refused and the corpus stays searchable.

Probe failures are distinguishable and each carries a meta.remediation payload in the same ACTION REQUIRED shape knowledge_search already returns for a missing embedding key: unreachable endpoint, auth rejected, non-OpenAI-compatible response shape, and dimension-not-supported-by-this-instance are four DIFFERENT messages, each naming the concrete next step.
The probe never leaks secrets: the endpoint URL is echoed in errors and posture reports, the API key never is. A test asserts no key material appears in any error body, log line, or audit entry.

The probe is bounded and cannot be used as an SSRF primitive or a DoS lever, WITHOUT re-blocking the local endpoints this epic exists to enable. It routes through the SINGLE egress policy module introduced in US-41.4 (AC-41.4.9) - an allowlist-aware wrapper over UrlGuard (e.g. UrlGuard.pin/2 gaining an allow: option fed by the deployment allowlist and the tenant's declared trusted endpoints) - never a second, divergent URL policy. Blanket 'reuse UrlGuard as-is' is explicitly NOT acceptable: UrlGuard.pin/1 blocks loopback and every private range, so an unmodified reuse makes a local endpoint unconfigurable. Outside an allowlisted/declared host the default denylist still applies, the probe has a short timeout, and it is rate-limited per tenant.

Default-off and non-breaking: a tenant that never sets embedding_base_url behaves exactly as today, including the mandatory-BYO-key behavior. No existing tenant is re-probed or re-embedded by this story.

test_cases.name: tenant endpoint overrides the server default on BOTH post paths
preconditions: tenant with embedding_base_url set to a stub local server
expected_results: both requests go to the tenant endpoint
the server-wide default is not contacted on either path

test_cases.name: probe records the dimension returned by the endpoint as PENDING
expected_results: settings persisted
tenant dimension recorded as 768
subsequent writes validate against 768

test_cases.name: dimension change on a populated corpus is refused without acknowledgement
steps: set embedding_base_url with no acknowledgement flag
expected_results: first attempt refused with a remediation naming the stale-row count
corpus still fully searchable after the refusal
second attempt records pending_dimension and enqueues the re-embed backfill
the new dimension activates only after the backfill completes

test_cases.name: unreachable endpoint fails closed with remediation
expected_results: error names the endpoint and the failure class
meta.remediation present and actionable
NOTHING persisted - prior settings intact

test_cases.name: each probe failure class is distinguishable
preconditions: four stub endpoints: refuses, 401s, returns non-OpenAI JSON, returns an unsupported dimension
expected_results: four distinct error codes and four distinct remediation texts - never one generic failure

test_cases.name: no key material leaks
steps: inspect error body, logs, audit entries
expected_results: endpoint present
key absent everywhere

test_cases.name: policy module governs reachability in both directions
preconditions: a tenant WITHOUT a declared/allowlisted local endpoint
steps: attempt to set a private-range endpoint as each tenant
expected_results: the undeclared tenant is rejected before any request with a clear error - no SSRF into the operator network
the declared tenant's private-range endpoint is probed successfully

test_cases.name: endpoint write stays role :user
steps: PATCH /tenants/me/llm-config with embedding_base_url at each role
expected_results: agent and orchestrator keys are refused
user key succeeds
no alternate route accepts the write at a lower role

technical_notes: Reuse Loopctl.Vault.Binary for nothing new here - the endpoint is not a secret and MUST be readable by egress_posture (US-41.4). Only keys stay encrypted. The endpoint is nonetheless written through a :user-role route because that PATCH also carries the keys.

The SSRF consideration cuts both ways: a local_only tenant NEEDS to reach private-range addresses (that is the point), while a hosted non-local tenant must not be able to probe the operator's internal network. Resolve this in ONE policy module (US-41.4 AC-41.4.9) consulted by the probe, provider calls, ingestion and webhook delivery - do not write a second, divergent URL policy here.
Record the probe result (endpoint, dimension, timestamp, outcome) in the audit log - US-41.7 builds the custody claim on top of exactly this record.
Ollama's OpenAI-compatible surface and HuggingFace TEI are the two reference targets; test against stubs shaped like both rather than assuming one vendor's response envelope.
SettingsCache has a documented staleness window; the pending/active dimension split must be read through a path that cannot serve a stale ACTIVE dimension to an in-flight embedding job.
